title: How Much of a Real Workload Can LLM-Generated GPU Kernels Actually Reach?
abstract: arXiv:2609.21058v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language models can now write GPU kernels that outperform PyTorch. We evaluate five model configurations on KernelBench level 1 and find that a frontier model produces correct kernels for 91.1% of problems and independently verified speedups on 22 of 56, including three convolutions, with a median of 1.235x. Open-weights models are far behind: the best reaches 30.4% correct with three verified speedups and solves zero convolutions.   We then ask a question the literature does not: what fraction of a real model's wall clock do such kernels govern? Profiling seven workloads across three domains, we find the addressable fraction ranges from 8.9% to 58.2%. On transformers, 80-86% of runtime is spent in cuBLAS GEMM and FlashAttention, bounding realistic end-to-end improvement at roughly 1%, and the fraction shrinks with model scale. On recommenders it is 58.2%, concentrated in a single embedding kernel. We introduce DLRM-Bench, 12 recommend

translated_title: LLM生成的GPU内核实际能触及真实工作负载的多大比例？
translated_abstract: 语言模型如今能够编写出超越PyTorch的GPU内核。我们在KernelBench level 1上评估了五种模型配置，发现前沿模型能够为91.1%的问题生成正确的内核，并在56个问题中的22个上获得了独立验证的加速，其中包括三个卷积运算，中位数加速比为1.235倍。开放权重模型则远远落后：最好的模型仅达到30.4%的正确率，只有三个经验证的加速，且无法解决任何卷积问题。随后，我们提出了文献中未曾探讨的问题：这些内核实际支配了真实模型挂钟时间的多大比例？通过对三个领域七个工作负载的剖析，我们发现可寻址部分的范围为8.9%到58.2%。在Transformer上，80-86%的运行时间花在cuBLAS GEMM和FlashAttention上，这将现实的端到端改进限制在大约1%左右，且该比例随模型规模增大而缩小。在推荐系统上，这一比例为58.2%，集中在单个嵌入内核中。我们提出了DLRM-Bench，12个推荐……
tldr: 该论文首次量化了LLM生成GPU内核在真实工作负载中的实际影响力——尽管前沿模型能为91.1%的KernelBench问题生成正确且经加速验证的内核，但这些内核仅能触及真实负载8.9%-58.2%的运行时间，在Transformer上端到端改进被限制在约1%，为此作者提出了针对推荐系统的DLRM-Bench基准。
en_tdlr: This paper is the first to quantify the real-world impact of LLM-generated GPU kernels—while frontier models produce correct, speedup-verified kernels for 91.1% of KernelBench problems, these kernels only address 8.9%-58.2% of real workloads' runtime, bounding end-to-end improvement to roughly 1% on transformers, motivating the introduction of DLRM-Bench for recommender systems.
